strengths: Phase discriminated union carries exactly the data each state needs; stale-attempt check (task.phase.attempt === attempt) uniformly covers cancel, timeout and late settles
Transaction + deferred event queue keeps the documented event order even when listeners re-enter the scheduler (nested calls' events land after the outer step's events)
Binary heap ready queue with lazy invalidation; iterative cycle search; Object.fromEntries for __proto__-safe ctx.deps; thorough option validation

Outstanding test suite: controlled/scripted harness, timer accounting, global-timer and Date.now spies, unhandled-rejection trap via macrotask, re-entrancy and ready-moment tests, claimed mutation script
weaknesses: Zero comments or docstrings in src; transaction/flush/pump interplay (flushing guard, moment counter, idleBefore loop) must be learned from NOTES.md
Cycle detection walks the whole reachable graph on every add (O(n) per add, O(n^2) for long chains), and dependenciesSucceeded re-scans deps on every release instead of counting
Cascade cause uses BFS-nearest dependency while add-time cancellation uses first-in-deps-order, a small inconsistency the notes admit
Single ~450-line file; the inline heap could have been a reusable module

bugs: findCycle in internal.ts is recursive and copies the path on every step ([...path, node]); adding to the end of a long dependency chain (~10k) overflows the stack and is O(n^2) per add
dispatch() picks the next task by linearly scanning the queued Set, so draining n queued tasks is O(n^2)

finish() emits the failure/cancel event before cascade() changes dependents' states, so a failure listener observes dependents still 'waiting' although they are about to be cancelled (inconsistent with the 'state first' story elsewhere)
strengths: Compact and straightforward; operate()/dispatchAndCheckIdle depth pattern is easy to follow
busy flag makes onIdle() called from the last success listener resolve after the idle event, a thoughtful edge
Attempt-token approach and stopAttempt/clearBackoff keep timer hygiene correct; abort-listener re-cancel guarded in attemptFailed
Reasonable docstrings on methods and a NOTES.md that lists decisions and confirms them with the PO
weaknesses: Flat Task bag of mutable fields (attemptToken, controller, timeoutTimer, backoffTimer, value, error) rather than a state-carrying structure; invariants between them are implicit
Several very long lines (doomedBy lookup, validation) hurt readability
Thinner tests: no unhandled-rejection or global-timer hygiene checks, no deep-chain or re-entrant-from-run scenarios, no __proto__ dep
Unsubscribe by indexOf removes only the first registration of a duplicated listener

bugs: In failAttempt, when a timed-out attempt's abort listener synchronously cancels the task, the 'retry' event is still emitted afterwards for an already-cancelled task (Y guards this case; Z does not)
strengths: Best algorithmic choices: unmet counters give O(1) readiness, forwardRefs map handles late deps, cycle search short-circuits unless an existing forward reference to the new id exists, generic Heap for dispatch; all graph walks iterative and a 20k-chain test proves it
Commit-then-emit discipline: states, cascade, slot release and abort are all applied before any event, so listeners always observe final states
Clean module boundaries (Emitter, Heap) with docstrings on fields and methods; defensive TypeError validation of id/run/deps
Focused tests with expectNoUnhandledRejections in every file, snapshot-emit semantics, self-cancel from run, randomized 300-task priority ordering, deep cascade
weaknesses: Rejects timeoutMs: Infinity where the other two accept it as 'no timeout' (design choice, but less lenient)
Stale cancelled entries linger in the heap until popped
NOTES.md points to an external redacted spec path for the full decision record
No test spies on global setTimeout/Date.now to prove the clock is the only time source

result.rationale: Z and X are both high-quality and close; Z edges ahead on design because of its O(1) readiness counters, forward-reference index, cycle-check short-circuit and reusable Heap/Emitter modules, plus a commit-then-emit discipline that makes listener-visible state trivially consistent. X compensates with the most careful event-ordering machinery under re-entrancy and by far the strongest test suite, but its source has no comments, its cycle search is linear per add, and its cascade-cause rule is inconsistent with its add-time rule. Y is acceptable and readable but structurally weaker: a linear-scan dispatch, a recursive path-copying cycle search that will overflow on long chains, flat mutable task records, events emitted before cascade state changes, and a thinner test suite.
